runbook_entries.question: How do the 22-agent live-task pointers stay in sync?
runbook_entries.answer: The heartbeat wrapper ~/workspace/gear-ledger/bin/gear-ledger-heartbeat.js derives each agent's pointer from the store: newest in_progress task else newest assigned task, formatted SHORT:tsk_id, one write per agent. Old path frozen. Present-pointer IDs are URN-prefixed (MUSE_CWI:tsk_...); tasks array carries bare IDs - match on the tail after the last colon.
runbook_entries.source: AGENTS.md 2026-09-22 + wrapper source read live; 22/22 pointers OK

runbook_entries.question: What is the memory read/write standing law?
runbook_entries.answer: Every task begins with memory.js read agent:X and ends with durable claims written (claim/source/date/confidence). read agent:X returns ONLY the shared pool + that agent's own namespace. Cross-agent teaching uses memory.js writeshared (single copy only).

runbook_entries.question: What is the memory->anchor cycle law?
runbook_entries.answer: After EVERY conversation entry: memory write -> git push to cwi-agent-memory -> offchain-anchor per agent -> offchain-verify. Memory never left UNANCHORED overnight. EAS off-chain attestations (EIP-712, chainId 84532), hash-chained via refUID; bodies never on-chain. Mainnet anchoring needs Black's per-batch signature - no agent key, no exceptions.

runbook_entries.question: What gates a TAG CITY deploy?
runbook_entries.answer: No build deploys without CWI_Visual's signed-off screenshot comparison (deployed frame vs locked key art). The look is a hard gate equal to tests and FPS. Debug overlays never ship in production.

runbook_entries.question: What is the synthetic-only art rule?
runbook_entries.answer: FINAL LAW (Black, 2026-09-22): no real-art uploads of any kind - not crops, not full art, nothing derived from the locked key art - to any external service, no exceptions, ever. Synthetic placeholders only. Constraint lives in the spawn brief itself.

runbook_entries.question: What is the encryption-at-rest workflow?
runbook_entries.answer: GPG AES-256 symmetric via the CWI-docs passphrase. Round-trip verify (decrypt -> sha256 match -> shred temp copy) BEFORE deleting plaintexts. Decrypt to /tmp only for local machine work; wipe temp plaintext after use; passphrase never in briefs, logs, or repos; external-facing agents get synthetic placeholders only.

runbook_entries.question: What is the no-downgrade law?
runbook_entries.answer: Never degrade graphics to the Atari age. Every visual lane ships modern, high-quality rendering or does not ship. When a build risks looking downgraded: reroute the process, research precedent, rebuild - never ship the downgrade.

runbook_entries.question: What are the truth rules?
runbook_entries.answer: 'Verified or it didn't happen.' Never fabricate adoption, traffic, rights, placements, metrics, etc. No agent reports a zero to Black without a fix - zero is an internal kill signal, never a deliverable upward - and faking a non-zero is the unforgivable failure.

runbook_entries.question: Why can't we trust the GitHub Contents API response body?
runbook_entries.answer: The Contents API returned wrong bytes (797 vs true 536) for 3 blobs while reporting the correct blob sha. Authority hierarchy: git/blobs > contents/sha > contents/content-field. Take the sha from Contents, fetch bytes from git/blobs.

runbook_entries.question: How do kill rules and checkpoints work?
runbook_entries.answer: Intervention checkpoints at 50% and 75% of every project window: diagnose the gap, change the actions, re-execute. Loops close by results, not expiry. Every play: predicted conversion with error bars, measurable proof, numeric kill line.

runbook_entries.question: What is the standing identity rule?
runbook_entries.answer: The project/company identity is Cumulative Web Inc - nothing else. No launches under Black's personal name or any other label; CWI logo on everything. His personal Facebook is reads-only; subscriber email blasts stay off without explicit approval.
